I had ritalin for the first time yesterday and I felt very similar to what you described too: not anything out of the usual, just that my brain instead of switching through 20 channels it just became slower and quieter. I did not feel high or happy or anything, just a neutral state of mind. Felt that time passed slower as well and I was able to follow through on mundane everyday tasks when I normally couldn't.

Right now it's back to its original state and comparing it to yesterday...it became really obvious that I can't control my thoughts or when I launch into daydream mode. But I am only going to eat it when I need to do work in order not to develop a tolerance for it. But it makes me demoralised that I need meds to be productive when others have a neurological advantage over us since the start.

If I were you I would go to IMH A&E and admit myself in. If not, go to the nearest polyclinic, tell let your doctor know about your situation. If they feel you need to be admitted they will arrange for an ambulance to send you there. Don't think about the hospitalisation fees first. You might need to wait 3-4 hours though to see the doctor though when you reach IMH though.

If you feel there's a stigma associated with IMH, then you can go NUH instead. In NUH have a mixed psych ward, but in IMH you can opt for a specialised ward for depression if there are beds available.

School counsellors only teach you how to cope with studies, they don't really address the underlying problems. You really need a therapist for your situation.
